summary: Yukio Sakamoto (1899–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Tohoku University, learning under Taiken Kimura, Daito Shimaji, and Nichien Fukami. He held professorial posts at Toyo University and served as president of Rissho University.

Yukio Yamanaka is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied as a graduate student at Kyoto University (attested 1996) and served as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).

Yuko Kamishima is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Indiana University Bloomington, the University of Cambridge, and the University of Tokyo, and under Ekai Kawaguchi. She held posts at Waseda University and Ritsumeikan University.
Yuko Matsuda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College. She held a post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, attested in 2001.

Yuko Yokochi is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Groningen under Minoru Hara, Katsuhiko Kamimura, and Hans T. Bakker. She served as associate professor (attested 2002) and professor (attested 2013–2021) at Kyoto University.
Yulian Zeng is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University, studying under Kirill Solonin and traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Yumi Katayama is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She studied as a PhD student at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) under supervisor Kenyo Mitomo (attested 2013).
Yumi Nakamoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who was a graduate research student at Ryukoku University (attested 2014) and served as an open recruitment researcher there in 2012.
Yumiko Ishihama is a scholar of Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University from circa 1982 to 1989 and held a post there around 1997.

Yun Ji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a PhD in Chinese literature from Fudan University in 2006 and held a post as librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).

Yun-hua Jan (1923–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He was a research fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953 and later served as a professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).
Yungfen Ma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed her PhD at Columbia University (attested 2011) under doctoral supervisor Chün-fang Yü.
Yunxi Wang (1926–2014) was a sinologist. He studied at Fudan University from circa 1947 to 1951 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1951 to 2014.

Yuri Levada (1930–2006) studied at Moscow University's Department of Philosophy (~1947–1952). He held posts at Moscow State University, the Institute of Sociology, VTSIOM, the Levada Center, and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences.
Yuri Parfionovich (1921–1990) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under George de Roerich and traditional teacher Bidia Dandaron.
Yusen Kashiwahara (1916–2002) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Otani University and later served as a professor there from circa 1961 to 1987.

Yusho Miyasaka (1921–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Chizan College and Tohoku University under Shoko Watanabe, he held posts at Koyasan University, Nagoya University, Chisan Denpōin, and Shuchiin University.

Yusho Wakahara is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami and held posts at Hanazono University (attested 1987) and Ryukoku University as assistant professor and professor (attested 1987–2013).
Yutai Ikeda (1934–2025) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post at Otani University and served as emeritus professor at Doho University from circa 1977 to 2005.

Yutaka Hirata (1931–2013) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He earned a doctorate from Kyushu University, later serving as professor emeritus there, and held posts at the Nara National Research Institute and Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University.
